The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement, not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University.


For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements.


Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

Major Specific Criteria


This articulation agreement displays lower-division course requirements specific to the major. Cal State LA lower-division course numbers range from 1000 - 2999. Students are advised to seek advisement from a counselor when planning to transfer to CSU Los Angeles and refer to the University Catalog to learn more about this major and its features. Additional admissions criteria for the major can be found on the Major Specific Criteria campus website. Please note that admissions requirements can vary by term so check back to see if there are any changes.

Program Overview

The Bachelor of Science degree in Physics, which requires a total of 120 units, may be used as preparation for graduate work or as a qualifying degree for professional employment. An Astronomy option provides substantial background for students planning graduate study in that field.

Programs in physics and astronomy are built on a foundation of high school studies in mathematics and physical sciences. For completion of a Bachelor of Science degree program in 8 semesters, high school preparation is recommended in physics, chemistry, geometry, trigonometry, and algebra (two years).

Student participation in research is strongly encouraged.

Program Requirements

  • The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Physics is 120 units, of which 79  are in the major.

    1. General Physics Option: A flexible path that prepare students for a wide range of careers in science, technology, and engineering, as well as for graduate study in physics and related disciplines. 
    2. Astronomy Option: A concentration for students planning to pursue graduate studies or careers in astronomy, space science, or similar areas.

  • Some of the required major classes can be double counted to fulfill University GE requirements. Consult with an advisor for the specific number of units required in all areas of the degree including GE and free electives.
  • Students must earn a minimum grade of C or higher in all courses used to meet major requirements.

  • Honors Program
    • The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers an honors program for qualified students. Students may apply in their junior year after completing PHYS 2100, PHYS 2200, PHYS 3300, and PHYS 3400.
    • Candidates must maintain a B (3.0) grade point average both in their major and overall.
    • Completion of the honors program requires 2 units of independent, research-oriented study (PHYS 3960) and presentation of the work in a colloquium.
    • Graduation with honors in Physics is conferred upon those students whom the faculty of the department deem qualified after presentation of the colloquium. Diplomas and transcripts of honors program graduates are designated: “Graduated with Departmental Honors in Physics.”
